E1.evidence: Public issue #166 (maintainer gavanderhoorn, 2017-04-05) with an error log from Travis: "unknown macro name: xacro:motoman_sda10f" while running roslaunch-check on motoman_sda10f_support/test/launch_test.xml, and the maintainer's diagnosis: "`sda10f.xacro` is trying to instantiate a macro called `motoman_sda10f`, but that doesn't exist, so `roslaunch` tests for that top-level xacro fail." Fix commit 90a9464 ("Fixed issue #166, added tests to ensure it is fixed").

units_identified: xacro (the processor that evaluates the files)
E2.evidence: Step 1: the only candidate pair is the motoman_sda10f_support package (whose top-level sda10f.xacro includes its own urdf/sda10f_macro.xacro) and the xacro processor. The two xacro files are one unit: they ship in one package and are not separately deployable ("a node and its own launch file are one unit" applies by analogy). Step 2: the failure is a name mismatch entirely inside that one package: sda10f.xacro calls `<xacro:motoman_sda10f prefix=""/>` while sda10f_macro.xacro at the same revision defines `<robot ... name="sda10f">` with no macro of that name ("The macro is actually called `sda10f`"). Any correct xacro processor would report an unknown macro, so the failure does not depend on an assumption between the package and its processor; the fix (90a9464) edits only files inside motoman_sda10f_support (defines `<xacro:macro name="motoman_sda10f" params="prefix">` and a compatibility `sda10f` macro). Ineligible: internal.

ineligible_reason: internal: the top-level sda10f.xacro instantiates a macro name (`motoman_sda10f`) that the macro file in the same package does not define (`sda10f`); both files are one unit, and the defect would surface with any correct xacro processor. The fix changes only motoman_sda10f_support. Context worth recording: PR #164 notes "I did verify that this is not an issue in Indigo. Apparently xacro naming was not a checked as closely?" and "I'm not sure why this is suddenly a problem. That file (`sda10f.xacro`) hasn't changed since it was originally committed.", i.e. a stricter xacro on Jade exposed the latent name defect; that exposure is not an interface change of xacro but the package's own error becoming visible. The same commit also fixes prefixing inside the package (`${prefix}base_link`, `${parent}` in arm_macro.xacro, PR #169 for kinetic), which are further internal changes, not interface conditions.
